clue.text: Chance outcomes with respect to numbers

parts.note: 'for' can mean 'as regards', as in 'for my part'
musical numbers are songs or tunes

explanation.surface: A statistician describes random results in terms of the figures involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' looks mathematical but means pieces of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunes are what chance deals out to a person, the luck that befalls them.

clue.text: Get to know about male meeting places set up

parts.note: 'he' is the male pronoun

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, a place for meeting and debate

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that men's clubs have been established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' signals reversal in a down clue; fora is the classical plural of forum.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to come to know about it; the phrasal verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Major defeat later rectified in court

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters of later are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A big loss in a lawsuit is put right later by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rectified' rearranges LATER to ATERL, which goes 'in' WOO. 'Court' looks legal but means woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final battle became a byword for a crushing, decisive defeat.

clue.text: Volcanic stuff found in southern Cairo, oddly

indicators.note: oddly signals that these letters appear in a strange arrangement

explanation.surface: Volcanic material turns up in the southern part of the Egyptian capital, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but rearranges S plus CAIRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoria is the cindery, porous rock fragments thrown out by a volcano.

clue.text: Plant left inside shelter

indicators.note: inside places the letter for left within the word for shelter

parts.note: cover is shelter, as in 'take cover'

explanation.surface: A plant has been left in a greenhouse or shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant of the pea family, with trefoil leaves.

clue.text: It may contain your fortune — what eventuates is how this 22

definitions.text: It may contain your fortune — what eventuates is how this 22

parts.words: It may contain your fortune — what eventuates is how this 22
parts.note: a fortune biscuit holds a slip with your fortune, and with 22 (crumbles) the phrase 'that's the way the ... crumbles' means that's how things turn out

explanation.walkthrough: 22 across is CRUMBLES, completing the saying about fate: what happens is just the way the biscuit breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune biscuit is a sweet baked treat holding a printed prediction, and the idiom names it.

clue.text: Male with tie on that's reckoned to bring luck

parts.note: an ascot is a broad neck tie or cravat

explanation.surface: A man wearing a tie is believed to be a good-luck charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept as a charm believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Money-raising actions offering 50/50 chances of success

definitions.text: Money-raising actions offering 50/50 chances of success

parts.words: Money-raising actions offering 50/50 chances of success
parts.note: flipping coins literally raises money into the air, and heads or tails is an even chance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Money-raising' sounds like fundraising but means lifting coins into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Flips of a coin, each giving an even chance of heads or tails, are what the clue describes.

clue.text: Adopted a stance in court — speaks out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters of court and speaks are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A defendant posed in the courtroom and spoke when not permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges COURT SPEAKS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a posture deliberately, for show, is the idiom for taking up a stance.

clue.text: Kind of luck that we discover, finally, in charming schoolboy

parts.note: pot luck is a kind of luck

indicators.note: finally picks the end letters of the words that, we and discover

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a type of good fortune found in an enchanting boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes T, E and R. 'Charming' means casting charms: Harry is a boy wizard at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry of the book series is a young wizard pupil who casts spells, literally a charming schoolboy.

clue.text: Supposedly lucky people seen in part of eye hospital

parts.note: the iris is the coloured part of the eye

explanation.surface: Fortunate patients are seen in the eye department of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'the luck of the Irish' credits that nation with good fortune.

clue.text: Wrong about good omen

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes around the letter for good

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken regarding a favourable portent.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a token or indication of what is to come.

clue.text: Some of our leave disallowed, as 5 across occasionally is

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of our holiday has been refused, which happens now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is CLOVER: rare clover plants with an extra leaflet are thought lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover usually has three leaflets; an occasional plant has one more, a famous lucky find.

clue.text: Fortuitously, in accordance with so-called lady's wishes

definitions.meaning: by chance, as things happened to turn out

definitions.text: in accordance with so-called lady's wishes
definitions.meaning: Lady Luck is chance personified, so this is as she wishes things to be

explanation.walkthrough: Lady Luck is the personification of chance, so her wishes are what fortune decides.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'by chance', saying events happened as fortune willed.

clue.text: Not cultivated prior to being guided

parts.note: until means up to the time of, i.e. prior to
led is the past tense of lead, to guide

explanation.surface: Something was left wild before someone showed the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that has never been ploughed or tilled is uncultivated.

clue.text: Ran edition in unlucky position?

parts.note: walking under a ladder is said to be unlucky, so in this down clue ED sits under the ladder

explanation.surface: A newspaper printed an edition and found itself in a bad spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue ED written below LADDER is 'in unlucky position', under a ladder. 'Ran' is what tights do.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights or stockings that ran have developed a ladder, a vertical line of broken stitches.

clue.text: Begins with supposed sources of luck — about time!

indicators.note: about means the stars go around the letter for time

parts.note: astrology credits the stars with shaping our luck

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with lucky charms, exclaiming that it's high time.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to begin, so the plural verb matches 'Begins'.

clue.text: See 13
A post, possibly, that you'll be lucky to get out of

definitions.text: that you'll be lucky to get out of

parts.note: a spot made tight (drunk, so jumbled) could read as post, and 'possibly' flags that it is only one such outcome

explanation.surface: A job vacancy that one would be fortunate to escape from.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'tight' means drunk, an anagram signal, so 'A tight SPOT' could turn into 'A POST'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky predicament or fix is something you are lucky to escape from.

clue.text: Rely on luck being good on promenade

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece is placed on top of the next

parts.note: to promenade is to stroll or amble

explanation.surface: Someone trusts to fortune while walking well along the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a chance and trust fortune is to gamble.

clue.text: A long shot for a better singer

definitions.text: A long shot for a better
definitions.meaning: a bet on three horses where all must win, a long-odds wager for a punter
a boy soprano, the highest voice in a choir

explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not a superior singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a three-race accumulator bet and a high boy's voice.

clue.text: No-win situation, something that's decided by luck

definitions.meaning: a game ending level, with no winner
a lottery or raffle in which prizes go by chance

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tied game and a lottery-style prize selection.

clue.text: Chef initially discovers the truth about sweet dishes

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word Chef

parts.note: to rumble someone is to find them out, a British informal sense

explanation.surface: A cook finds out what is really going on with the puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumble' in British slang means to see through someone's deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit desserts topped with a rubbly baked flour-and-butter mix are classic puddings.

clue.text: High score with dice, within maximum for Romans

definitions.meaning: with two dice, the second-highest possible total
the letters XI sit inside the word maximum, and XI is a Roman numeral

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: Roman XI, found in the middle of 'maximum', is the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Two dice give totals up to twelve, so this number is a high throw.

clue.text: Pirate providing what fortune-teller requires in hand

definitions.meaning: Long John, the pirate of Treasure Island
a fortune-teller asks you to 'cross my palm with' this metal

explanation.walkthrough: Fortune-tellers traditionally ask clients to cross their palm with a coin of this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both Stevenson's one-legged buccaneer and the precious metal for crossing a palm.

clue.text: As part of genteel destiny, most like to succeed

indicators.note: As part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A refined fate makes someone a likely high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means inherit, not achieve: the first-born child inherits a title.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-born child is the one in line to inherit, i.e. to follow a parent.
